title: Label the feeling
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What is the other person feeling right now, in one phrase?
Jose said that chapter 3 is about not denying or ignoring emotions: good negotiators identify and influence them. They are not obstacles, they are means.
A student said that labeling is stating what they are feeling. Jose said: it is spotting their feelings, turning them into words, and calmly repeating them back, validating by acknowledging.

Jose said you can say: it seems like you are a little frustrated; it sounds like you are having a bad day; it looks like you are upset with the situation. He said to keep a back door, because they may say do not tell me what I feel.
He gave a positive label: it seems like people put you in front of this deal because you are the only one able to get it done, and I am happy it is you I am working with.
He added that after a label you can stay silent, and that we are all tempted to fill silence by talking.
A student said that it is all about being subtle: if you are too straightforward and it is not how they feel, they will feel you are putting words in their mouth.
Jose said: you cannot fake it. The whole thing is being authentic and really paying attention.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the last emotion you saw in someone.
Write the label: it seems like.
Write a positive label for your next meeting.
Write how long you will stay silent.

check.q: What did Jose say good negotiators do with emotions?
What did Jose say to keep after a label?
What did a student say about being too straightforward?
choices: They feel you put words in their mouth

recap: Label the feeling softly. Leave a back door. Stay silent.
